# Skill: Frontend Design

# Frontend Design

Start from the user's task, not from decoration.

## Before coding

- Identify the primary user goal and the one primary action on the screen.
- Inspect the existing design system: `client/src/index.css`, Tailwind tokens, shadcn/Radix components, spacing, radii, and typography.
- Reuse existing components and classes. Do not introduce a second visual language.
- Check the current page at mobile and desktop widths before changing layout.

## Hierarchy and layout

- One clear H1, scannable sections, and a visible primary action.
- Use a consistent spacing scale and type scale. Avoid arbitrary pixel values.
- Mobile-first. Test at 360, 768, and 1280 px minimum.
- Avoid fixed widths/heights that clip content. Let text wrap; truncate only where intended.
- Keep touch targets at least 44x44 px.

## States

Every data-driven view needs:

- Loading: skeleton or spinner that matches final layout.
- Empty: explain what is missing and offer the next action.
- Error: human message, retry action, no raw stack traces.
- Disabled, hover, focus, active, and selected states.
- Long content, narrow viewport, and slow network behavior.

## Accessibility

- Semantic HTML first: `button`, `a`, `label`, `nav`, `main`, headings in order.
- Every input has a label. Errors are announced and tied to the field.
- Keyboard navigation works. Focus is visible and logical.
- Contrast at least 4.5:1 for body text.
- Use `aria-*` only when native semantics are insufficient.
- Respect `prefers-reduced-motion`.

## Tailwind and visual quality

- Use existing color tokens and CSS variables. No random hex values.
- Consistent radius, border, shadow, and icon sizes.
- Avoid generic AI styling: gradient soup, emoji as icons, centered everything, giant hero copy, excessive glassmorphism.
- Use real content or realistic placeholders, not lorem ipsum.
- Motion should clarify state changes, not delay them.

## Verify visually

- Run the app and load the page.
- Check console errors and failed requests.
- Use the browser/Playwright skill for a real render, responsive check, and screenshot when layout matters.
- Test keyboard-only navigation and one small viewport before declaring done.

## Rules

- Do not redesign unrelated screens.
- Do not add a dependency for a basic layout or icon.
- Do not ship a screen with only a happy-path state.
- Preserve existing behavior and routes unless asked to change them.

## Objective
- User asked to clone/pull the latest repo changes locally, run the project, then fix the liquid-glass design: search bar style/contrast issues in Home and refraction lag during scroll.

## Requirements
- Preserve glassmorphism/liquid-glass look while fixing contrast.
- "El tono blanco en la barra de busqueda hace invisible unas palabras. Optimiza y repara el diseño conservando contrastes."
- Fix refraction delays on scroll.

## Decisions
- Repo already existed locally with remote `https://github.com/Netherstar44/ViaNovaIA`; used fetch + `git pull --ff-only` instead of fresh clone.
- Search bar kept as a bright iOS-style glass surface in every palette, with dark ink, rather than making text adapt to dark mode.
- Root cause of sticky navbar failing: unlayered `.lg-surface { position: relative }` overrode Tailwind `sticky`; moved it into `@layer components`.
- Scroll optimization: only fixed/sticky surfaces repaint on scroll; surfaces that travel with the page skip repaint. Removed 20 fps throttle, now rAF-coalesced.
- Cached base color sampling for anchored surfaces; early geometry rejection in `paintMedia` to reduce per-frame cost.

- Pulled `main` from `020f299` to `c80f3d7` (8 commits), `npm install` done.

- `client/src/lib/liquid-glass-webgl.ts`: WebGL glass engine; scroll anchoring, rAF repaint, base cache, media paint optimization.
